groups.title: Angular Reactive Forms internals
groups.question: You are building a task form with a title, due date and a username that must be unique on the server. Explain how Angular's reactive forms represent the form and run validation.

followUps.FormControl, FormGroup, and FormArray: t: How do FormControl, FormGroup and FormArray relate?
followUps.Synchronous and async validators: how va: How do async validators differ from sync validators?

evidence.text: A FormControl tracks one input's value and validity.
A FormGroup groups named controls, such as a whole form.
A FormArray holds a list of controls whose length can change.
Synchronous validators run on every change and return errors or null.
Async validators, like checking a username with the server, return an Observable or Promise.
Async validators run only after the sync validators pass, and their state is pending while they run.

groups.title: Angular change detection and OnPush strategy
groups.question: Your task board slows down as it grows, and the first page load downloads code for every feature. Explain how OnPush change detection and lazy loading help.

followUps.OnPush change detection: only check on n: When does an OnPush component get checked for changes?
followUps.Lazy loading feature modules to reduce t: How does lazy loading reduce the first download?

evidence.text: By default Angular checks every component after every event.
OnPush checks a component only when an input reference changes, an event happens inside it or an async pipe emits.
This requires immutable updates, because changing an object in place keeps the same reference.
A lazy route loads its feature code only when the route is visited.
The initial bundle is smaller, so the app starts faster.
The build splits each lazy feature into its own file.

notEnough: Only saying lazy loading loads later.

groups.title: Building reactive forms with validation in Angular
groups.question: Your task form shows red errors before users have typed anything, and building controls by hand is verbose. Explain how you would build and display the form's validation.

followUps.Displaying field errors: touched, dirty,: When should a field's error message appear?

evidence.text: FormBuilder creates groups and controls with a short syntax.
Validators are listed with each control's initial value.
The result is the same form model as building it by hand.
Show errors only when the field is invalid.
Wait until the user has touched the field or tried to submit.
Showing errors on an untouched form frustrates users before they start.

notEnough: Only saying you show errors when invalid.

groups.title: Dynamic form arrays and state management patterns
groups.question: Your task form needs a list of subtasks that users can add and remove, and the selected task must be shared across several components. Explain how you would handle both.

followUps.FormArray for dynamic subtask lists with: How would you let users add and remove subtask fields?
followUps.NgRx signals or BehaviorSubject for cros: When is a service with a BehaviorSubject enough and when would you reach for NgRx or signals?

evidence.text: New controls are pushed onto a FormArray.
removeAt removes the control at an index.
The template loops over the array's controls to show each field.

notEnough: Only saying you use a FormArray.

evidence.text: A service with a BehaviorSubject is the simplest way to share state.
A state library helps when updates become complex and need to be traced.
Such libraries add structure and code, so they should be adopted when the need is real.

notEnough: Only saying NgRx is for big apps.
